# Verdict: REVISE ## Overall Assessment The LiveSearch component has a solid accessibility foundation — proper label association, a well-structured `aria-live` region, sensible arrow-key navigation, and a clear Escape-to-dismiss flow. However, it contains one **critical focus-visibility failure** (explicitly removing the focus outline on result links) and a **fundamental ARIA pattern conflict** (declaring `role="listbox"`/`role="option"` on a list of navigable links, with focus landing on the links rather than the options). The ARIA roles are effectively dead code that misleads screen reader users about the interaction model, and the CSS focus treatment will be invisible to keyboard and low-vision users in multiple rendering conditions. --- ## Pre-commitment Predictions Before reading the code, I predicted the following for a live-search / combobox-style component: | # | Prediction | Result | |---|-----------|--------| | 1 | ARIA pattern mismatch — listbox/option roles on elements that are actually links | **CONFIRMED** — `role="option"` on `
  • `, focus on `` | | 2 | Missing `aria-activedescendant` or `aria-selected` | **CONFIRMED** — both absent | | 3 | Focus visibility issue on the result items | **CONFIRMED** — `outline: none` in CSS | | 4 | Focus loss when results re-render under the focused item | **CONFIRMED** — no guard in `handleInputChange` | | 5 | `aria-controls` pointing to a non-existent ID when list is unmounted | **CONFIRMED** — conditional render removes the target | No major surprises. The component's strengths (label, live region, Escape handling) were not predicted as risks and are correctly implemented. --- ## Critical Findings (blocks access) ### C1. Focus indicator explicitly removed on result links **Evidence:** CSS, `ul[role="listbox"] a:focus` rule: ```css ul[role="listbox"] a:hover, ul[role="listbox"] a:focus { background: #eff6ff; color: #1d4ed8; outline: none; /* ← focus outline removed */ } ``` **User group impacted:** Keyboard-only, low-vision, and screen-reader + keyboard users. **Why this matters:** `outline: none` removes the browser's default focus indicator. The only remaining focus cues are: - Background shift from `#ffffff` → `#eff6ff` (contrast ratio ≈ **1.05 : 1** — effectively invisible) - Text color shift from `#1f2937` → `#1d4ed8` (a color-only change) In **Windows High Contrast Mode**, both the background and text-color shifts are overridden by the system palette, leaving **zero** focus indication. At **200% zoom**, the 1.05 : 1 background delta is imperceptible. A keyboard user tabbing or arrow-keying through results cannot tell which item is focused. **WCAG citations:** - **2.4.7 Focus Visible** — "The keyboard focus indicator is visible." - **2.4.13 Focus Appearance** (WCAG 2.2) — requires a minimum 2 px perimeter with a 3 : 1 contrast change against adjacent colors. The 1.05 : 1 background delta fails by a factor of ~3. - **1.4.1 Use of Color** — color must not be the sole means of conveying focus state. **Confidence:** HIGH. The CSS is unambiguous. **Fix:** ```css ul[role="listbox"] a:focus { background: #eff6ff; color: #1d4ed8; outline: 2px solid #2563eb; /* restore a visible outline */ outline-offset: -2px; /* keep it inside the padding box */ } ``` Or, if the design system prefers a box-shadow approach: ```css ul[role="listbox"] a:focus { background: #eff6ff; color: #1d4ed8; outline: none; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px #2563eb; /* 2px inset ring, 3:1+ vs #eff6ff */ } ``` Verify the chosen indicator meets 2.4.13: ≥ 2 px perimeter, ≥ 3 : 1 contrast against both the focused background (`#eff6ff`) and the adjacent unfocused background (`#ffffff`). --- ## Major Findings (significantly degrades experience) ### M1. ARIA pattern conflict: `role="listbox"` / `role="option"` on a list of navigable links **Evidence:** Component JSX, results list: ```jsx
      {results.map((result, index) => (
    • {result.title}
      • ))}
    ``` **User group impacted:** Screen-reader users (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver). **Why this matters:** This is a **WAI-ARIA APG Combobox** declaration with **link-list behavior**. The conflict manifests in three ways: 1. **Focus lands on the ``, not the `
  • `.** The `handleKeyDown` and `handleResultKeyDown` handlers call `.focus()` on the `` element. Screen readers announce the focused element — they hear *"Getting started guide, link"* — not *"Getting started guide, option, in list box."* The `role="option"` and `role="listbox"` are never announced because focus never lands on those elements. The ARIA roles are **dead code**. 2. **`aria-label` on the listbox is never announced.** The label `"Search results: 4 items"` is on the `
      `, but focus is on the `` children. The user never hears the container context. 3. **Inconsistent interaction model for AT users.** `aria-autocomplete="list"` + `aria-expanded` + `aria-controls` on the input declare a combobox. APG combobox options are **selectable, non-focusable items** (divs/spans). Here, options are **focusable links** that navigate on Enter. A screen-reader user who has learned combobox behavior (from other sites) will expect `aria-activedescendant` tracking and Enter-to-select, but instead gets native link navigation. The declared pattern and the actual behavior disagree. **WCAG / APG citations:** - **WAI-ARIA APG Combobox pattern** — options must be `role="option"` elements that are **not** links; focus stays in the combobox input; `aria-activedescendant` tracks the active option. - **4.1.2 Name, Role, Value** — the role declared (`option`) does not match the element's actual behavior (navigable link). **Confidence:** HIGH. The code unambiguously places `role="option"` on `
    • ` while focusing the child ``. **Fix (recommended — simplest, most correct):** Remove the listbox/option roles. The items are links in a list; let them be that. The `aria-live` region already announces the result count. Arrow-key navigation is a progressive enhancement on top of native link semantics. ```jsx
        {results.map((result, index) => (
      • handleResultKeyDown(e, index)}> {result.title}
        • ))}
      ``` Keep `aria-autocomplete="list"`, `aria-expanded`, and `aria-controls` on the input — these are still valid and useful. Remove `role="listbox"` and `role="option"`. The `aria-label` on the `
        ` becomes a simple list label, which is correct. **Alternative (if the team wants a true combobox):** Remove `href` from options, change `` to `
        `, add `aria-selected`, add `aria-activedescendant` on the input, keep focus in the input at all times, and handle Enter to call `window.location.href` or `onSearch(result.url)`. This is more code and more testing surface. --- ### M2. Missing `aria-selected` on options (if retaining listbox pattern) **Evidence:** No `aria-selected` attribute on any `
      • ` in the component. **User group impacted:** Screen-reader users. **Why this matters:** Per the WAI-ARIA APG Listbox pattern, each `role="option"` must have `aria-selected="true"` or `aria-selected="false"`. Without it, screen readers cannot communicate selection state. If the M1 fix (remove listbox/option roles) is applied, this finding is **moot**. **WCAG / APG citation:** WAI-ARIA APG Listbox pattern — `aria-selected` is a required state. **Confidence:** HIGH (conditional on M1 not being fixed). **Fix:** If keeping the listbox pattern, add `aria-selected={index === activeIndex ? 'true' : 'false'}` and track `activeIndex` in state. If removing the listbox pattern (recommended), this finding is resolved. --- ### M3. Focus loss when results re-render and the focused item is removed **Evidence:** `handleInputChange` (lines with `setResults(mockResults)`) and the conditional render `{results.length > 0 && (...)}`. **Scenario:** User types "get" → 4 results appear → user presses ArrowDown twice → focus is on result #2 ("API reference" — wait, "get" wouldn't match that; let me use a realistic scenario). User types "tr" → results filter to 1 item ("Troubleshooting common errors"). User presses ArrowDown → focus on that single result. User types "trou" → results re-filter. If the focused result is still in the list, fine. But if the user types "troublesh" and the mock data only has one match, it stays. The real risk is with a live API: user is on result #3, types a character, the API returns a different set where result #3 no longer exists. React unmounts the `
      • ` and ``. Focus falls to ``. The user is stranded. **User group impacted:** Keyboard-only users, screen-reader + keyboard users. **Why this matters:** The user is mid-interaction (navigating results) and suddenly loses focus to the document body. They must re-tab from the top or re-press ArrowDown from the input. This is disorienting and breaks the interaction flow. **WCAG citation:** **2.4.3 Focus Order** — focus should move in a logical, predictable order. Losing focus to `` is neither logical nor predictable. **Confidence:** MEDIUM. The mock data makes this hard to trigger, but with a real API it is a realistic scenario. The code has no guard. **Fix:** ```jsx const handleInputChange = (e) => { const value = e.target.value; setQuery(value); if (debounceRef.current) clearTimeout(debounceRef.current); debounceRef.current = setTimeout(async () => { const newResults = await performSearch(value); // If focus was on a result link, return it to the input if (listRef.current && listRef.current.contains(document.activeElement)) { inputRef.current?.focus(); } }, 300); }; ``` Or, if using the combobox pattern (focus always in input), this issue is structurally eliminated. --- ## Minor Findings (friction but workaround exists) ### m1. `aria-controls` references a non-existent ID when results are empty **Evidence:** `aria-controls="search-results-list"` on the input. The `
          ` is conditionally rendered: `{results.length > 0 && (...)}`. When `results` is empty, the element is not in the DOM, and `aria-controls` points to a missing ID. **Impact:** Low. Most screen readers handle dangling `aria-controls` gracefully. `aria-expanded="false"` correctly communicates the list is closed. **WCAG citation:** 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (minor — the reference is technically invalid). **Fix:** Either keep the `
            ` in the DOM with `hidden` / `inert` when empty, or conditionally set `aria-controls`: ```jsx aria-controls={results.length > 0 ? "search-results-list" : undefined} ``` ### m2. No loading / busy state during debounce **Evidence:** The 300 ms debounce window has no `aria-busy`, `role="status"` "Searching…", or visual spinner. The live region only announces the final count. **Impact:** Very low. 300 ms is below the perceptual threshold for most users. With a real API (1–3 s), this becomes more relevant. **WCAG citation:** 4.1.3 Status Messages (informative). **Fix (for real API):** Add `aria-busy="true"` on the results container during the fetch, or announce "Searching…" in the live region before the results arrive. --- ## Enhancements (best practice not met) - **e1.** No `role="combobox"` on the input. `aria-autocomplete="list"` implies it, but being explicit helps older AT. Add `role="combobox"` if keeping the combobox framing. - **e2.** The `
            ` wrapper has no semantic role. If this component appears in a page without a `
            ` landmark, the search area is not discoverable via landmark navigation. Ensure the page provides `
            ` or `
            `. - **e3.** `autoComplete="off"` prevents the browser from offering previously-used search terms. Some users (especially those with motor impairments who rely on autocomplete) may benefit from `autoComplete="on"` or a specific token like `autoComplete="section"`. Consider whether "off" is truly necessary. - **e4.** No `prefers-reduced-motion` media query. The component has no animations, so this is a non-issue today, but if a fade-in or slide-down transition is added to the results list, it must be gated behind `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`. --- ## What's Missing (gaps) | Gap | Why it matters | |-----|---------------| | **No guard for focus loss on re-render** (M3) | Keyboard user stranded at `` when the focused result is filtered out | | **No `aria-activedescendant`** | If the combobox pattern is retained, AT cannot track which option is "active" while focus is in the input. Moot if the listbox/option roles are removed (M1 fix) | | **No `aria-selected`** (M2) | Required by the listbox pattern; absent | | **No `inert` or `aria-hidden` on the results list when closed** | The list is conditionally rendered (removed from DOM), so this is handled. ✓ No gap. | | **No skip-link context** | Component-level; the page should provide one. Not a component defect. | | **No `lang` attribute visible** | Component-level; the page `` is responsible. Not a component defect. | --- ## Multi-Perspective Notes | Perspective | Alarm Level | Notes | |-------------|-------------|-------| | **Screen reader** | **HIGH** | ARIA roles (listbox/option) are declared but never announced because focus lands on `` children. The `aria-label` on the listbox is inaudible. The live region correctly announces result count. After the M1 fix (remove listbox/option), the screen-reader experience is clean: "4 results found" + a list of links. | | **Keyboard-only** | **HIGH** | Arrow-key navigation works well. Escape works. **But `outline: none` on result links (C1) means the user cannot see which result is focused.** This is the single most impactful defect. | | **Low vision (200% zoom, high contrast)** | **HIGH** | Focus indicator (C1) is invisible in high-contrast mode. The 1.05 : 1 background delta is imperceptible at any zoom. Text color shift is the only cue, and it is color-only. | | **Cognitive** | **MEDIUM** | Clear label, clear result list, clear Escape-to-dismiss. No confusing state changes. The interaction model (type → arrow down → navigate) is intuitive. No issues. | | **Vestibular & motion** | **LOW** | No animations, transitions, or auto-playing content. No risk. | | **Auditory access** | **LOW** | No media elements. No risk. | | **Environmental contrast** | **MEDIUM** | Input text `#111827` on `#fff` ≈ 16.7 : 1 ✓. Label `#374151` on `#fff` ≈ 8.0 : 1 ✓. Result link text `#1f2937` on `#fff` ≈ 14.7 : 1 ✓. Focused link text `#1d4ed8` on `#eff6ff` ≈ 5.2 : 1 ✓. All text contrast passes. The **focus indicator** contrast fails (see C1). | --- ## Verdict Justification **REVISE** — not REJECT, because the component's core interaction model (type → debounce → results → arrow-key navigate → Enter to go) is sound and the live-region announcement is well-implemented. The label, `type="search"`, `aria-autocomplete`, `aria-expanded`, and `aria-controls` are all correct and useful. However, two issues must be resolved before shipping: 1. **C1 (Critical):** The `outline: none` on result links is a hard WCAG 2.4.7 / 2.4.13 failure. Keyboard and low-vision users cannot identify the focused result. This is a one-line CSS fix. 2. **M1 (Major):** The listbox/option ARIA roles on a list of links create a false pattern declaration. Screen reader users are told (by the ARIA tree) that they are in a combobox with selectable options, but the actual elements are navigable links. The fix is to **remove the roles** and let the semantic `
              ` / `
            • ` / `` structure speak for itself. The `aria-live` region already handles the announcement that the ARIA roles were (incorrectly) supposed to provide. **Path to ACCEPT:** - Fix C1 (restore a visible focus indicator on result links meeting 2.4.7 + 2.4.13) - Fix M1 (remove `role="listbox"` and `role="option"`; keep the semantic list of links) - Fix M3 (guard against focus loss on re-render) - M2 is resolved by M1 - m1 and m2 are minor and can be addressed in a follow-up After those fixes, the component's accessibility design is coherent: a labeled search input with a live-region announcement, a semantic list of links, arrow-key progressive enhancement, and a clear Escape-to-dismiss flow. That is a clean, defensible pattern. --- ## Open Questions (unscored) 1. **Is this component used in a context where the results list could have 50+ items?** If so, the `max-height: 320px; overflow-y: auto` on the listbox means the focused item could scroll out of view. Does the implementation call `.scrollIntoView()` on focus? I don't see it in the code. If not, add `element.scrollIntoView({ block: 'nearest' })` in the focus handlers. 2. **Is the `onSearch` prop used by a parent to navigate?** The component receives `onSearch` but never calls it. If the parent is expected to handle navigation on result selection, the current `` approach bypasses it. Clarify the intended navigation mechanism. 3. **Is this component rendered inside a `
              `?** If so, pressing Enter in the input will submit the form (native behavior) in addition to navigating the focused link. If the form has no `action` or `onSubmit` handler, this is a no-op. If it does submit, the user may get an unexpected page reload. Verify the form context. 4. **Does the design system have a global `:focus-visible` style that this component's `outline: none` is overriding?** If so, the fix for C1 should use `:focus-visible` (not `:focus`) to avoid showing the outline on mouse-click focus, and the design system's token should be used for the outline color/width.
